name: L.B. Foster Company

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Small Pittsburgh maker and distributor of track components, friction-management products, rail monitoring tech, precast concrete and steel bridge/pipe products; founded 1902, two segments.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: 2025 sales $540.0M: Rail, Technologies and Services 57% (rail distribution, insulated joints, transit fasteners, friction management, track monitoring) and Infrastructure 43% (precast buildings, steel bridge products, pipe coating). 9M-2026 Rail sales +20.2%.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: No customer above 10% of 2025 sales; in 2024 one Rail customer was about $71.8M (about 13.5%), unnamed. Buyers are short lines, transit agencies, contractors, Class Is, and government-funded projects.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: 2025 sales: US $481.4M (89%), UK $32.4M (6%), Canada $19.4M, other $6.7M. UK is the weak spot (product lines being exited: AMH 2025, Tew 2026).

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Project and contract sales plus product sales, sealed bids for transit; not recurring. Orders are lumpy; Q3-2026 backlog $234.7M (Rail $126.4M -9.8%, Infrastructure $108.3M +1.0%). Aftermarket friction-management service is a small recurring piece.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Gross margin 21.1% (2025), operating margin 4.1% (2025) and 6.0% in Q3-2026: thin. Capex $10.4M (1.9% of sales). Working capital swings: operating cash flow 2022 -$10.6M, 2023 $37.0M, 2024 $22.6M, 2025 $35.6M. Q3 guidance hit rate not disclosed (company gives no formal guidance in the filings read).

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Buys steel, cement, aggregates (mostly domestic suppliers), epoxy and electronics; also finished/semi-finished steel products from domestic and some foreign producers; 'a number of vendor options' and no single supplier named, so no disclosed single point of failure. Foreign purchases face tariffs and anti-dumping duties. Pass-through is partial and not stated: Q3-2026 Rail gross margin fell 320bp to 19.6% on mix while sales rose 32%. Signal tags: steel price, tariffs, dollar (import cost), oil (epoxy/lubricants), rates (customer financing).

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Patents and trademarks in friction management, track monitoring and precast; CXT brand in precast buildings; installed base for friction management. Doing differently now: exiting low-margin UK lines (AMH, Tew), buying Dulworth precast operating assets for $52.2M cash (closed 2026-10-28), new Florida precast plant.

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: B2B industrial supplier; no consumer usage; market cap about $0.4B. Customers would switch among vendors for commodity track accessories.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Competition 'in each product line' from different groups of companies; share data not disclosed. Rail Products Q3 sales +54.6% and orders +55.0%, while Friction Management orders -10.2% and sales -9.0%; no share series available.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Dulworth adds precast capacity; Florida plant ramping; Steel Products orders +508% in Q3 on prior-year cancellations; Rail Products strong. But total backlog is down, and growth is project-timing driven, not structural. Little evidence of segments scaling unpriced.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: FCF (operating cash flow less capex) 2025 $25.2M, 2024 $12.8M, 2023 $32.4M, 2022 -$18.2M. Rough ROIC about 7-8% (NOPAT about $16M on about $214M capital; my calculation), below a 10% cost of capital. Debt $28.7M at 9/30/26, then $52.2M Dulworth funded from cash and revolver. Repurchased 1.017M shares for $23.6M since 2023 (about $23 average), none in 2026. CEO owns 2.2%; PSUs pay on Economic Profit Improvement and Adjusted EBITDA. Activist 22NW holds 11.3%.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Track components are needed and spending follows Class I, transit and state funding, but the business is a small, price-taking cyclical. Operating income was -$7.2M in 2022 and $21.9M in 2025; sales roughly flat, $540M in 2025 vs $531M in 2024. Not losing relevance; thin edge.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: Item 4.02 filed 2024-10-07 (gain classification error of $3.477M after SEC comments; material weakness at 12/31/2023). Remediated: 10-K FY2025 concludes internal control effective. CORRESP/UPLOAD letters were in Aug-Nov 2024; none found since. No NT filings. Heavy activist presence but no related-party issues seen.

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Boom +; Overheat 0 to + (steel and wages push cost, volume helps; surcharge-style pass-through is not disclosed); Stagflation -; Slowdown - (lower freight and transit capex, project delays, small cap with a revolver). Rate sensitivity: revolver is floating, partly swapped ($20M swaps). Dollar: UK/Canada exposure is about 10% of sales.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Exposed to federal infrastructure funding, shutdown delays, Buy America style content rules, and steel tariffs and anti-dumping duties named in risk factors. No pending regulatory docket found.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: $37.78 gives market cap about $397M; pro forma net debt about $74M (debt $28.7M less cash $7.2M plus $52.2M Dulworth) so EV about $471M, 12x LTM EBITDA (about $38.6M, my calculation) and 13.7x 2025 EBITDA. Reverse DCF at 10% discount rate, 3% terminal: needs about 4% (on $29M pre-interest FCF) to 6% (on $25M) FCF growth for 10 years. Own last 5 years FCF is erratic (2022 -$18M to 2023 +$32M) so no clean growth rate. Price assumes steady growth from a lumpy base: no cushion. Own 5-year and peer multiples: not pulled.

status_reason: Quality is C (thin 4-6% operating margin, lumpy cash flow, ROIC below cost of capital), so it cannot survive; no kill-switch rule holds, and the price leaves no cushion.

feedback.note: Rail Products orders +55.0% and sales +54.6% in Q3-2026 supports the strong US freight/maintenance-spend read in AAR data; Rail backlog -9.8% and Friction Management orders -10.2% show no broad acceleration. Infrastructure steel orders had prior-year cancellations. Nothing yet confirms the Slowdown turn.
